audit.why: Mel out-ranges immobile Galio in the 1v1 all game; his value is the level-6 global roam window. Content, packet chart and prose agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides were blanket 'Skill' and phases[4].why claimed level 6 is Mel's execute countdown while content win[4] and the packet chart give 6 to Galio (Hero's Entrance).
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is a 180s global that flips tempo at 6 even though the 1v1 stays Mel's.
audit.corrected: Row 4 flipped to Galio with a matching why; other rows aligned to Mel per content.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two applicable interactions absent: Colossal Smash's auto-reset is the burst tell, and Justice Punch cuts the retreat of a dash-less Mel (hold Flash for the wall). Cooldowns field had no numbers.
audit.why: Kit flags: P autoReset, E terrain/dash; missingInteractions lists both.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — the execute threshold turns your chip war into a countdown he can see.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is a 180s global: if you shove and he vanishes, he's ulting a sidelane — ping and match.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1, 7 at max — his only engage; while it's down he cannot touch you. - Shield of Durand is 18s, Hero's Entrance 180s. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Solar Snare during his wind-back cancels the punch — the step-back before the charge is your cue to fire the root early.

edits.before: That’s Galio’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Colossal Smash's auto-reset wind-up is the tell — inside his reach that bonus AoE hit lands free.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Volleying is a stand-still cast — with Justice Punch (11s) up he punishes the animation, so weave volleys behind minions or after his E.

edits.before: Track Galio’s Justice Punch: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Galio’s Justice Punch: his dash knockup — you have no dash, so hold Flash for the wall, not the damage.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Galio wins by cutting your retreat with Justice Punch, taunting your dive answers, and out-roaming you with Hero's Entrance.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Q-volley the last-hit and keep W glowing — Winds of War is a projectile Rebuttal returns, so his only poke feeds your chip war.
